claim_verdicts.evidence: PlaceOrderLong.cs @ stage-0 lines 4-5: `// One method that checks, prices, saves and notifies. Four reasons to change` / `// one place, and no name for any of the four.` Joined across the line break, the lesson's quote "Four reasons to change one place, and no name for any of the four." is exact.

Opinion/definition; no official doc under versions.yaml governs it. The ledger's condition ("this matters when code is expected to change after it first works") is absent from the lesson, which states it unconditionally: section 4 "Where each piece of work lives decides that cost for every change that comes later"; summary 5 "it sets the cost of every later change". Design shapes, not solely decides, change cost.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Where each piece of work lives is a large part of what a later change costs: it decides how much you must read and re-check before you can make the change safely.

issues.quote: The saving and email lines read `totalVnd` too, so a pricing change reaches them as well.
issues.text: False of this code. PlaceOrderLong.cs:32 is `Console.WriteLine($"sending an email to customer {customerId}");` — it does not read totalVnd. Only the saving line (31) and the return (34) read it after the fee. Also an unlisted claim.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The saving line and the returned message read `totalVnd` too, so a pricing change reaches them as well; the email line only uses `customerId`, but it still sits in the same method you must re-read." Add the corrected sentence to `claims`.

issues.text: The diagram shows totalVnd flowing into 'notify the customer', but the notify line (PlaceOrderLong.cs:32) never reads totalVnd. The same section's "every step after the discount reads the discounted value" is also false for the email line.
issues.fix: Delete the edge `T --> N` (keep `T --> S`, optionally add a node for the return value). Change "every step after the discount reads the discounted value" to "the steps after the discount read the discounted value".

issues.quote: the fee, the saving line, the email line and the return — because they all share that one variable
issues.text: The email line does not use totalVnd (PlaceOrderLong.cs:32 prints only customerId), so it does not 'share that one variable'. The suggested answer teaches a false reading of the code.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "the fee, the saving line and the return — because they all read that one variable — and the email line too, since it sits in the same method."

issues.text: Fill answer set is incomplete: it accepts the English thousands separator "2,000,000" but not the Vietnamese one "2.000.000", which the vi text of the lesson and quiz use (q1/q5 vi: 2.000.000). A vi learner typing it is marked wrong.

issues.quote: the four still share one body and one variable
issues.text: Option d explanation: notification (email line) does not read totalVnd, so the four jobs do not all share one variable. Key is correct; the explanation repeats the section 5 error.
issues.fix: Change to "the four still share one body" (en) and "bốn việc vẫn chung một thân" (vi).

issues.quote: It is a one-character edit to the discount
issues.text: Changing `10` to `5` replaces two characters with one; it is not a one-character edit. Repeated in section 6: "a one-character pricing edit". Unlisted claim.
issues.fix: Use "a one-number edit" in section 2 and "a one-number pricing edit" in section 6.

issues.quote: `Place` gave correct answers both before and after the discount edit
issues.text: Whether dropping the fee is 'correct' is exactly what is unknown — the code says nothing about which total the fee should use. What is true is that Place did what its code says both times.
issues.fix: Replace with "`Place` did exactly what its code says both before and after the discount edit". Same wording change in q2 explanation ("gave correct results").

issues.quote: Where each piece of work lives decides that cost for every change that comes later.
issues.text: Unconditional; the ledger (claim 5) itself adds a condition the lesson drops. Placement shapes change cost; it does not alone decide it. Same in summary line 5: "it sets the cost of every later change".
issues.fix: Use claim 5's suggested_text in section 4; summary 5: "Design is the set of choices about where each piece of work lives, and it shapes how much every later change costs."
